claims.statement: The console (web/console) is an Angular 22 application built with standalone components, signals and zoneless change detection, and it wires no Angular Router: main tabs and per-backend sub-tabs are switched by plain signals (appConfig provides only error listeners and fetch-backed HttpClient; bootstrapApplication starts the standalone App).

The console is organised into four strict layers: root shell (app.ts), per-router panel (backend-pane.ts plus child components), a root-provided Injectable service layer owning all HTTP boundaries and shared state, and Angular-free pure-function modules (config-ops, connections-model, flow-model, node-form, share-link, line-diff, group-board-model, rule-model, util) that carry all structured logic.

The App root shell owns: the `active` signal for main tabs ('b<n>' backend panels, 'edit' rule editor, 'pool' shared panel) with an activeIndex computed that clamps to the backend list; per-backend sub-tab memory (panes signal, restored via initialTab input and tabChange output, reset on reload); the storage status dot driven by ShareHealthService.start() probing /share/health every 30s; the origin trust banner comparing location.origin to PAGE_ORIGINS; and the footer showing CONSOLE_VERSION plus a sing-box version probed via ClashService.

Only the active backend tab is rendered: app.html materialises activeIndex() as a one-element @for array with an explicit `ai !== null` guard (index 0 is falsy), because a nested @if inside the backends loop created the pane twice on every tab switch.

BackendPane hosts the seven sub-tabs (PaneTab: overview/groups/connections/flow/logs/rules/config) and centralises per-tab side effects in enterTab: the log WebSocket is opened only while the logs tab is active (?token= query auth, sing-box accepts nothing else, 300-line buffer, auto-scroll only when pinned to bottom) and is closed on tab leave or destroy; the runtime GET /rules table is lazy-loaded on first entry; overview/connections/flow/config acquire their own data on mount.

BackendPane hosts the cross-tab pending-save bar: flow-page dialog edits are staged in ConfigDraftService and survive sub-tab switches until 保存并重启; runSave() drives the SaveProgressDialog with estimated step timing over the single blocking apply call, classifies failures onto the failing step with an actionable hint, and a missing-credential outcome (needCreds) opens SshCredDialog and auto-retries the save after credentials are stored.

All console services are Injectable with providedIn:'root'. BackendsService persists the backend list and global key in localStorage (clashBackends/vaultKey) with memory-only drafts and keyFor(b) = per-backend key falling back to the global key; ClashService is the direct-browser clash_api client using Authorization: Bearer for REST and ?token= for WebSockets because sing-box only reads the query parameter; VaultService owns /rule-set/* reads and POST /publish with X-Vault-Key plus a front-end validate() pre-check mirroring the server's key whitelist; RouterService is the /router/* client sending X-Vault-Key = keyFor(backend) (server accepts VAULT_KEY or the router's clash secret) with apply(config, expectSha) as the optimistic-lock write; ShareHealthService probes /share/health and exposes /share/config|probe|import and public-rules preview/apply.

LiveStatService is the sole /connections poller: subscribe(backend, ms?) registers consumers, same-backend subscribers share one polling chain whose interval is the minimum across subscribers (header 2s, connections 2s, flow 1.5s); each snapshot carries api and at so consumers filter by backend and de-duplicate by timestamp; the last unsubscribe stops the timer and clears snap; fetches are skipped while document.hidden and a visibilitychange listener catches up on return.

The connections page feeds LiveStatService snapshots through connections-model's ConnTracker.apply, which diffs adjacent snapshots into rate/idle/closed rows (rate = byte delta over interval, idle = time since last byte growth, vanished ids become closed rows capped at CLOSED_LIMIT 500) and de-duplicates processing via the snapshot's at timestamp.

serializeConfig(doc, like) re-serialises an edited ConfigDoc using the original file's indentation width (probed from line 2), CRLF/LF line endings and trailing-newline style, so structured edits produce minimal diffs instead of reformatting the whole file; it is the single serialization path for both staging chains (ConfigPane.enterReview and ConfigDraftService.save), and residual diff noise is limited to hand-tightened lines being normalised.

config-ops.ts is the structured-editor library for the whole sing-box config.json: accessors for outbounds/endpoints/route.rules/route.rule_set, node add/update/delete with deleteImpact analysis, addGroup, addRuleSet plus addRuleSetRef(s) with previewRuleSetRef/ruleInsertPoint (domain rules before IP buckets, new refs before the final fallback rule), moveRule, the applyRuleGroups/applyRegroupRows regroup engine, pruneOrphanGroups (keeps at least one group), normalizeOutboundTags (uppercase outbound tags with full reference rewriting, bucket tags untouched), and validateDoc as a front-end pre-check whose authority remains sing-box check on the router.

Edit/create dialogs (rule-set ③, group ④, node-create ⑤, rule-set-create, group-create, rule-regroup) never write to the network themselves: they clone the base ConfigDoc, apply pure-function edits and emit a new document via docChange, leaving the staging chain to the host — flow-page hosts call ConfigDraftService.stage (cross-tab pending bar → 保存并重启) while the config page calls ConfigPane.enterReview (serialized text + diff review → 应用并重启). node-create-dialog is shared verbatim by the flow page's ⑤ column and the config page; rule-set-create-dialog writes definition plus reference in one step but intentionally does not create NAS bucket files, checking /rule-set/index and directing the user to create and publish buckets in the rule editor first.

ConfirmService.ask({title, body, details, danger}) returns Promise<boolean>, queues concurrent requests and settles each independently; it exists because browsers can block further native dialogs, after which confirm() silently returns false — dangerous for destructive operations. ConfirmDialog renders it on a native <dialog> with showModal() (ESC and backdrop-click cancel, danger prompts focus cancel). ToastService.show/ok/error replaces alert() with a non-blocking bottom-right stack (auto-dismiss; errors stay 6.5s). Both are mounted once in app.html and driven only by their services.

The 配置 sub-page is a staged pipeline: a connection gate when no global clash key exists (credentials are submitted to the 99 host then cleared from page memory), reload() records original text + sha256 as the optimistic-lock base, structured edits and Monaco hand edits only touch the staging text, pending = raw !== original drives the yellow banner and lineDiff preview, check() runs /router/check (sing-box check on the router), and apply() blocks on JSON syntax errors, confirms validateDoc issues as a danger confirm, and posts /router/apply with expectSha — a 409/STALE answer means someone else changed the config and the user must re-read; success re-reads the base.

ConfigDraftService manages the flow-page draft: load(backend) fetches /router/config into originalText/originalSha/baseDoc and clears the old draft; stage(doc) holds the in-memory draft (cancel/refresh discards); save(backend) pre-checks SSH credentials on the 99 host (setting needCreds instead of a doomed apply), serializes with serializeConfig against originalText, applies with expectSha, and on success clears the draft and re-reads the base with 3 retries — persistent re-read failure degrades to a warn (配置已写回并重启成功…) rather than a false save-failure error.

The rule-editor main tab edits NAS rule buckets rather than the router: its file tree is the live /rule-set/index listing (buckets with a .json source only; .srs-only compile artifacts hidden), bucket names must match /^(rs-[a-z0-9-]+|bard-domains)$/, Monaco edits JSON with strict diagnostics, and publish posts to /publish — the server validates, compiles .srs, writes both files back to the bucket, and routers pull the remote rule-set on their ~60s cycle with zero restart.

The console builds with `npx ng build --base-href=/edit/`; production sets outputHashing:'all' so the output is a set of hashed files (main-<HASH>.js …), and deploy_console.sh replaces the whole remote page directory (backup → wipe → extract) because overwriting only index.html would break hashed asset references. The script also vendors Monaco (min/vs from npm pack) into /static/monaco/vs unless the remote VERSION file matches, and monaco-editor.ts loads the AMD loader from /static/monaco/vs at runtime — fully offline, no npm monaco and no CDN. Post-deploy checks verify /edit/ 200, /static/monaco/vs/loader.js 200, the hashed entry js 200, and /publish without key 401.

models.ts constants are load-bearing across service boundaries: CONSOLE_VERSION is the footer version (manually bumped per release); PAGE_ORIGINS must equal the Go service's allowOrigins in service/config.go and the routers' clash_api CORS whitelist (otherwise the browser blocks console↔router calls); LAT_LOW/LAT_MID (400/800 ms) are the single latency threshold pair consumed by util.latClass and flow-model.

Shared helpers are convergence points that components must extend rather than re-implement: util.ts owns fmtBytes (single B/K/M/G scheme), fmtRate/fmtMib, latClass/latText, ageText/ageClass, errMsg, isNetworkErr and the runPool concurrency pool (concurrency 6 for 全部测速); line-diff.ts owns the LCS row diff (DP matrix capped at 4,000,000 cells, at most 60 detail lines with full add/del counts); node-form.ts owns form validation/assembly (buildNode returns ok/error per protocol, formFromNode flattens for edit). This replaced per-component copies of byte formatting, latency classing, concurrency pools and the diff algorithm, shrinking config-pane.

The console has no component-level unit tests; `npm run test:ops` (test/run-ops-tests.mjs) bundles config-ops.ts and shared-pool.service.ts to ESM with esbuild and runs assertion modules in test/ops/*.mjs (fingerprint, pool nodes/rules/override, group-apply, cond-merge, string-rule-set), skipping fixture-gated cases when test/ops/fixtures/router-32.json (real node secrets, not committed) is absent. UI acceptance is a real-browser pass through gate → read → edit → stage → check → apply → revert after deployment, plus scripts/mock_clash.mjs which serves a fake clash_api and hosts the built console for data-shape-heavy pages like the connections browser.
